terms.comment: Greek σκελετός, “dried up”: in Apuleius a small carved figure of a wasted corpse, the only author Lewis & Short cites for the word. The sense of the bones as one frame is the modern anatomists’. Classical Latin has no single word for it and says ossa.

terms.gloss: a ghost; a skeleton as a figure of death
terms.comment: Properly a ghost or spectre; Petronius uses it of the jointed silver skeleton brought in at Trimalchio’s dinner.

sources: Lewis & Short: larva
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. skeleton.
